- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 0.5–1.5% per day).
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or introduce early mean-reversion trigger.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extrapolating from recent volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment-adjusted baseline).
